food.servingGuidance: Adult RDA: 40 mg/day (ICMR). Sources: amla (600 mg/100 g), guava, citrus, capsicum.
food.precautions: Diarrhea at >2 g/day. Kidney stones risk at very high doses. Increases iron absorption (helpful & harmful).
food.sourceNote: Wellness Catalog — NIH Office of Dietary Supplements

food.name: Vitamin D
food.description: Sunshine vitamin synthesized in skin; common deficiency in India despite sunlight.
food.usesBenefits: Calcium absorption, bone & muscle health, immunity, mood, possible autoimmune prevention.
food.servingGuidance: Adult RDA: 600 IU (15 µg)/day; 800 IU if >70 yr. Sun: 15–20 min arms/face mid-day. Sources: fatty fish, egg yolk, fortified milk.
food.precautions: Toxicity at >4,000 IU/day (hypercalcemia, kidney stones). Always supplement under guidance after testing 25-OH-D levels.
food.sourceNote: Wellness Catalog — NIH Office of Dietary Supplements

food.name: Vitamin E
food.description: Antioxidant vitamin protecting cell membranes from oxidative damage.
food.usesBenefits: Antioxidant, skin health, immune support, may protect against cognitive decline.
food.servingGuidance: Adult RDA: 15 mg/day. Sources: almonds, sunflower seeds, wheat germ, spinach.
food.precautions: High doses (>400 IU) increase bleeding risk and mortality in some studies. Stop before surgery.
food.sourceNote: Wellness Catalog — NIH Office of Dietary Supplements

food.name: Vitamin K
food.description: Vitamin for blood clotting and bone metabolism.
food.usesBenefits: Blood clotting (prothrombin), bone mineralization, vascular health.
food.servingGuidance: Adult AI: 90–120 µg/day. Sources: leafy greens (K1), fermented foods (K2), animal products (K2).
food.precautions: Interacts with warfarin — consistent intake crucial. Avoid high-dose supplements without monitoring if on anticoagulants.
food.sourceNote: Wellness Catalog — NIH Office of Dietary Supplements
